answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The velvet multiplier is published, charged in harbor, and umber lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3818 identities would post 1866 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
